title: Why We Have Seasons
objective: After this level you can explain that seasons come from Earth's tilt, not its distance from the Sun.
summary: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5°. Each hemisphere takes turns leaning toward the Sun, which is why seasons are opposite north and south.

cards.headline: Most people get this one wrong: summer isn't when Earth is closest to the Sun.

cards.fact: Earth is closest to the Sun in early January.
cards.context: That's the middle of winter in the Northern Hemisphere. So distance can't be what makes summer.

cards.headline: It's the tilt
cards.body: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5°. When your hemisphere leans toward the Sun, sunlight hits the ground more directly and days last longer, so more energy lands on each patch of ground. That's summer. Lean away, and the same sunlight arrives at a slant and spreads thin.

cards.headline: Opposite seasons
cards.body: Because the hemispheres lean opposite ways, December is winter in New York and summer in Sydney. Same planet, same distance, different lean.

cards.headline: Seasons: solved
learned: Earth is closest to the Sun in January

options.label: Earth's changing distance from the Sun
options.rationale: Earth is closest in January — northern winter.

options.label: Changes in the Sun's brightness
options.rationale: The Sun's output is nearly constant.

options.label: The Moon's position
options.rationale: The Moon affects tides, not seasons.

questions.explanation: Earth's ~23.5° tilt changes how directly sunlight hits each hemisphere through the year.

questions.prompt: It's July. What season is it in Australia?

options.label: Summer
options.rationale: July is summer in the north, so it's winter in the south.

options.label: It depends on the distance to the Sun

questions.explanation: The hemispheres tilt opposite ways, so northern summer is southern winter.

questions.prompt: Venus is hotter than Mercury (Level 3), and northern summer happens when Earth is farther from the Sun. What do both show?

options.label: Planets closer to the Sun are always hotter
Venus causes Earth's seasons
options.rationale: Venus has no effect on our seasons.

options.label: Earth's orbit is a perfect circle
options.rationale: It's slightly oval, but that isn't the point here.

questions.explanation: Venus's atmosphere traps heat, and Earth's tilt sets the angle of sunlight. In both cases something other than distance is in charge.
